details: A WhatsApp/Baileys library published under an unofficial scope (@trashcore/baileys, where the canonical package is @whiskeysockets/baileys) that covertly subscribes the running account to hidden WhatsApp channels. In lib/Socket/newsletter.js, inside makeNewsletterSocket(), two nested timers fire 90 seconds and then 95 seconds after the socket is created and silently issue newsletter FOLLOW queries (query_id 7871414976211147) with base64-encoded channel JIDs decoded to 120363420249672073@newsletter and 120363424020283759@newsletter. Both calls are wrapped in empty catch blocks — no log line, no configuration flag and no consent path — so the account follows channels the user never chose. The hook is reachable on every normal session: makeNewsletterSocket() is invoked unconditionally at module scope in lib/Socket/messages-send.js. The package also aliases its signal dependency to an unofficial implementation ("libsignal": "npm:@shennmine/libsignal-node") instead of the upstream package, hardcodes marketing/newsletter JIDs in lib/Socket/luxu.js and lib/Utils/messages.js (including 120363420757607688@newsletter), and fetches its runtime version config from a third-party GitHub repository at hxxps://raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com/kiuur/bails/master/src/Defaults/baileys-version[.]json. The shipped code contains no credential, token or local file access; the payload acts only through the authenticated WhatsApp session.
